heading: Customer deposits; interest; refund

diff_segments.text:
170 IAC 4-1-13 Customer deposits; interest; refund

(a) A utility may require a deposit from a residential customer only to secure payment of bills for service, and only where the customer has an unsatisfactory credit history as determined under the utility's approved tariff.

(b) The deposit shall not exceed one-sixth (1/6) of the estimated annual billing for the customer. The utility shall give the customer a written receipt that states the amount, the interest rate, and the conditions of refund.

(c) Interest on the deposit shall accrue at the rate set by the commission from the date of deposit and shall be credited annually or paid at refund.

(d) The utility shall refund the deposit, with accrued interest, after twelve (12) consecutive months of prompt payment, or upon termination of service after deduction of any unpaid final bill.

heading: Disconnection; prohibited disconnections; reconnection

diff_segments.text:
170 IAC 4-1-16 Disconnection of service; prohibited disconnections; reconnection

(a) A customer may request that service be discontinued on any date after giving the utility reasonable notice. The customer remains liable for service furnished until three (3) working days after the requested discontinuance date, or until the date the utility actually discontinues service, whichever is earlier.

(b) A utility may discontinue service without prior notice when a condition on the customer's premises is dangerous or hazardous to life, physical safety, or property, or when the utility has reasonable evidence of fraudulent or unauthorized use of electricity or of tampering with the utility's metering or regulating equipment. The utility shall document the specific basis for the discontinuance and, where practicable, leave written notice at the premises stating the reason.

(c) A utility
shall

not discontinue residential service for nonpayment where the customer has delivered, before the discontinuance date stated in the notice, a certificate from a licensed physician or public health official stating that discontinuance would be a serious and immediate threat to the health or safety of a person residing at the premises. The certificate postpones discontinuance for ten (10) days. The postponement shall be continued for one (1) additional ten (10) day period upon delivery of an additional certificate. The utility shall also offer a reasonable payment arrangement to any customer who demonstrates financial hardship.

(d) A utility
shall
may

not discontinue residential service for nonpayment (1) before 8:00 a.m. or after 3:00 p.m. prevailing local time; (2) on a day, or on the day preceding a day, on which the utility's business office is not open to the public; or (3) after noon on the day preceding a day on which the office is closed. This subsection does not apply to discontinuance under subsection (b).

(e) Except as provided in subsection (b), a utility shall not discontinue residential service for nonpayment unless it has mailed or personally delivered written notice to the customer at least fourteen (14) days before the proposed discontinuance date. The notice must state: (1) the amount past due; (2) the date on or after which service will be discontinued unless payment or an arrangement is made; (3) the telephone number and address at which the customer may arrange payment or dispute the bill; (4) the availability of the medical certificate postponement; (5) the customer's right to file an informal complaint with the commission's consumer affairs division; and (6) the information required by 170 IAC 4-1-16.6 regarding energy assistance during the winter period.

(f) A utility shall not discontinue service for nonpayment of charges that are the subject of an unresolved dispute filed under 170 IAC 16-1 where the customer is paying the undisputed portion of the bill.

(g) Where service has been discontinued, the utility shall reconnect service within one (1) working day after the customer has paid the past-due amount, made an acceptable payment arrangement, or otherwise remedied the cause of discontinuance, and shall not impose a reconnection charge that exceeds the charge on file in its approved tariff.

(Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission; 170 IAC 4-1-16; filed Mar 3, 2008, 3:20 p.m.: 31 IR 1722)

heading: Performance tests

diff_segments.text:
Source: IC 13-14-8

(a) This section applies to each person, facility, or filing described in performance tests.

(b) The responsible person shall maintain records, reports, and notices required by this section and shall make them available on request.

(c) Definitions used in this section are in section 2
of this part.
